svg.title: Nineteenth-century jihad states and Samori's empire
svg.desc: Map of West Africa with the approximate areas of states created by nineteenth-century jihads: the Sokoto Caliphate founded by Usman dan Fodio (jihad from 1804) in Hausaland; Masina (Hamdullahi) founded by Seku Ahmadu (from 1818) on the inland Niger delta; and the Tukulor empire of al-Hajj Umar Tall (from the 1850s) between the Senegal and the Niger. Samori Toure's Mandinka empire (from the 1870s) is also shown. Areas are approximate.
svg.text: Areas are approximate; borders changed constantly.
